observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly emits a 'JSC_THIS_TYPE_NON_OBJECT' warning when a @this annotation uses a typedef that includes null or undefined, even if the underlying type is an object.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves adding a call to 'restrictByNotNullOrUndefined()' in two locations: one in 'FunctionTypeBuilder' to properly validate the subtype relationship, and one in 'FunctionType' to ensure the resolved type of 'this' is correctly handled. These changes are essentially adding missing validation/normalization logic to handle nullable/undefined types correctly within the type-checking predicates, which fits the 'Checking' category.
evidence_used: The fix adds 'restrictByNotNullOrUndefined()' to the subtype check in FunctionTypeBuilder.
The fix adds 'restrictByNotNullOrUndefined()' to the resolution of 'maybeTypeOfThis' in FunctionType.
The bug report indicates that '@this' emits a warning when used with a typedef that includes null/undefined, even when the base type is an object.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the logic, the core issue is the failure to correctly validate the type (checking if it is an object while ignoring null/undefined), which is a predicate/validation error.
